organization: TiE (The Indus Entrepreneurs) -- a global nonprofit entrepreneurship network; TYE is delivered through independent, city-level TiE chapters worldwide rather than one central organization
location: City-chapter based (examples confirmed via chapter sites: Boston, Houston, Seattle, Atlanta, Washington DC, Delhi, Hyderabad, Singapore, London, Manchester, and others); Global Finals location varies by year
residency_requirement: Not stated as a formal rule, but effectively required in practice: the program is delivered through local in-person chapter cohorts, not a unified global online application.
international_eligibility: TYE is described as a 'Global Program' with 'over 20 chapters' (per one chapter page) to '35 chapters across the globe' (per tyeglobal.org's own Impact page) -- a genuinely global network, but structured as independent city chapters rather than one open worldwide entry point.
turkiye_accessible: unclear -- no TYE chapter in Turkey or Istanbul was found after directly checking tyeglobal.org and multiple individual chapter sites (Houston, Seattle, and others) and searching specifically for an Istanbul/Turkey chapter. TiE has chapters in many countries globally, but none confirmed in Turkey. No stated fallback/remote path was found for a student in a city without a chapter, unlike LaunchX's or Blue Ocean's more centralized models. This is a genuine 'unclear' rather than a confirmed exclusion.
age_requirement: One chapter's impact page mentions a past participant who joined 'around 12.5 years old' -- an anecdote, not a stated eligibility rule.
grade_requirement: 'Any 9th-12th grade student interested in entrepreneurship, STEM or business may apply to participate!' -- this phrasing was returned by a web search attributed to a TiE chapter page, but was NOT independently re-confirmed via a direct fetch of that exact chapter page this session, so it is recorded at medium (not top) confidence.
application_deadline: unknown, chapter-dependent -- the central tyeglobal.org page returned almost no operational detail (only a title/heading) when directly fetched.
program_dates: Global Finals historically described as held in June (per one chapter's description of a Seattle-hosted event); exact 2026-27 dates were not confirmed on any official page reached this session.
cost: unknown -- not found on any page reached
prize_or_stipend: '$10,000 in cash prizes' at the Global Competition, per a chapter page's own description -- not independently re-confirmed via direct fetch of a central rules page this session.
team_or_individual: Team-based -- teams form to 'launch startups'; one source describes teams of four, but this was not independently confirmed as a strict global rule.
selection_process: Local chapter cohort (classroom sessions on business/entrepreneurship modules) -> chapter-level Pitch Fest/Finals -> the winning team per chapter advances to the TYE Global Finals (described as a 'Pitch Fest' with 'conference, and learning summit').
official_application_url: unknown -- no unified global application form found; entry is via individual city-chapter pages (e.g. houston.tie.org/tye/, seattle.tie.org/tye/)
verification_status: LEAD -- the program's existence, general structure, and $10,000 global prize figure are corroborated across multiple independent TiE chapter pages, but the organization is decentralized enough (30+ independently-run city chapters, a very thin central tyeglobal.org page) that I could not pin down one canonical, current, verbatim eligibility/deadline/cost statement this session, and could not confirm or rule out Turkey access with confidence.
notes: Worth a dedicated future pass emailing tye@tie.org (an official contact address found on the global site) to directly ask whether a Turkey-based student can enter without a local chapter -- exactly the kind of question this decentralized website structure cannot answer on its own.

selectivity_evidence: None officially stated -- no acceptance rate was found published anywhere; described qualitatively elsewhere as competitive, but no number is recorded per the rule against inventing selectivity figures.
required_documents: An application form; a financial-aid request during the application if needed. No transcript or standardized-test requirement was found.
essay_required: Unclear -- application is described as motivation/curiosity-based, but the exact format (written application vs. interview vs. both) was not fully confirmed via direct official fetch this session.
test_requirement: None found ('doesn't require grades in the application process' per a secondary source)
source_urls: https://tks.vision/faq/ (direct fetch attempted, failed with a TLS certificate error)
https://www.join.tks.world/toronto (found via search, not independently fetched this session)
verification_status: PARTIALLY_VERIFIED -- age range, virtual-global accessibility, program duration/dates, and both pricing tiers with financial-aid availability are all confirmed via direct fetch of the official tks.world homepage. The exact admissions process (interview details), grade band, and the 65-country/100%-aid/30-scholarships figures come from search-engine synthesis of TKS's own materials rather than an independently re-quoted direct fetch this session (a fetch attempt to tks.vision/faq/ failed with a TLS certificate error).
notes: IMPORTANT SCOPE CAVEAT: TKS is explicitly broader than pure business/entrepreneurship -- its own description covers 'building projects with companies like Google and OpenAI ... mastering AI, biotech, and robotics.' Best framed to a student as a general deep-tech/innovation accelerator with a strong venture-building component, not a dedicated business-plan competition. It is also a significant PAID commitment (roughly $4,900-$7,390 total over 10 months before aid) combined with a genuinely selective application process -- exactly the 'selective admission AND pay-to-attend' combination the research brief asked to watch for; both facts should be shown to a student/family together, not just one.

canonical_name: Genc BizzTech (Bilim ve Teknoloji Tabanli Lise Girisimcilik Programi / Science and Technology-Based High School Entrepreneurship Program)
organization: Genc Basari Egitim Vakfi (Junior Achievement Turkiye), in partnership with Turkiye Is Bankasi
location: Turkey (nationwide, restricted to state science high schools); winning team travels to GEN-E in Latvia
citizenship_requirement: Not framed as a citizenship rule -- the operative gate is school type (see residency_requirement).
residency_requirement: 'Turkiye'nin 81 ilindeki devlet fen liselerinde ogrenim goren ogrencilerin katilabilecegi' = 'Students enrolled in state science high schools (devlet fen lisesi) across Turkey's 81 provinces [can participate]' (verbatim Turkish + translation, official gencbizztech.org FAQ). This is a school-TYPE structural barrier, not a general Turkish-residency rule: a Turkish student not enrolled in a state science high school (e.g. a regular Anadolu Lisesi or private-school student) does not appear to qualify based on this quote.
international_eligibility: Not applicable -- this is a domestic Turkish program. Its only international dimension is that the winning team represents Turkey at GEN-E 2026 in Latvia, described on the program's own site as 'Avrupa'nin en buyuk girisimcilik festivali' (Europe's largest entrepreneurship festival).
turkiye_accessible: yes, with a structural caveat -- this is itself a Turkish national program, so 'Turkey access' is not the relevant eligibility question. The relevant, non-obvious restriction is that it is open only to STATE SCIENCE HIGH SCHOOL students, not all Turkish high schoolers -- exactly the kind of structural access barrier the research brief asked to watch for, and it is stated in the program's own FAQ, not inferred.
age_requirement: Not separately stated; school-type enrollment is the operative rule.
grade_requirement: Enrollment in a 'devlet fen lisesi' (state science high school); specific grade-within-high-school not specified in the sources checked.
application_open: unknown for the next (2027) cycle. The 2026 cycle's own application window is reported by a secondary Turkish-language news/education-portal source (not the primary program site, whose own activity calendar was presented only as an image) as having closed 2025-12-21.
application_deadline: unknown for the next cycle; the already-concluded 2026 cycle's deadline (per a secondary source, not a directly-quoted official page) was 2025-12-21.
program_dates: 2026 cycle: application window closed Dec 21, 2025 (per secondary source); national final results announced May 2026 (per multiple Turkish news outlets); winning team eligible for GEN-E 2026 in Latvia.
cost: unknown -- no fee was found stated on either official page reached (gencbasari.org/gencbizztech/ was an incomplete 'coming soon' placeholder page at the time of this research; gencbizztech.org's FAQ did not mention cost).
prize_or_stipend: Winning team receives physical attendance at GEN-E 2026 (Latvia), a virtual-booth opportunity at the GEN-E virtual fair, and eligibility to compete for additional special awards there (verbatim-translated from the official gencbizztech.org FAQ: 'GEN-E 2026'ya fiziksel olarak katilim, GEN-E sanal fuarda stant acma ve ozel odullere basvurarak yarismaci olma imkani').
team_or_individual: 'Takimlar en az 2 kisiden olusmalidir' = 'Teams must consist of at least 2 people' (verbatim + translation, official gencbizztech.org FAQ)
selection_process: 'Turkiye'nin dort bir yanindan gelen yuzlerce fikir arasindan one cik ve Turkiye Finali'ne katilacak 10 fark yaratan ekipten biri olma sansini yakala!' = 'Stand out among hundreds of ideas from across Turkey for the chance to be one of the 10 teams that make it to the Turkey Final!' (verbatim + translation, official FAQ). The 2026 cycle specifically drew '472 takim' (472 teams) per Turkish news coverage of the concluded cycle.
selectivity_evidence: 472 teams entered the 2026 cycle nationally; 10 advanced to the Turkey Final (from Turkish news coverage of the concluded cycle's results, corroborating the program's own '10 teams advance' FAQ language).
required_documents: Not fully specified in the sources checked; a dedicated application form exists (gencbizztech.org/basvuru.php) but the specific required materials (business-plan format, video, etc.) were not confirmed.
recommendation_required: Unclear -- the program explicitly offers separate 'Ogrenci' (Student), 'Ogretmen' (Teacher), and 'Mentor' application tracks, suggesting a teacher/mentor is involved in a school's participation, though not confirmed as a hard per-team requirement.
source_urls: https://gencbasari.org/gencbizztech/ (incomplete placeholder page at time of research)
verification_status: PARTIALLY_VERIFIED -- the state-science-high-school restriction, team-size minimum, selection funnel (hundreds of teams -> 10 finalists), and the GEN-E Latvia prize connection are all directly quoted from the program's own official gencbizztech.org FAQ. The precise next-cycle (2027) deadline and any participation cost could not be confirmed: the official activity-calendar was an image (not machine-readable text), and cost was not mentioned on any official page reached. The 2025-12-21 deadline figure for the already-concluded 2026 cycle comes from a secondary Turkish-language news source, not a directly-quoted official page, and is presented with that caveat.
notes: Genuinely new find for ORYN, not present anywhere in the existing research corpus (which already covers a separate, non-tech-specific 'GencBizz' / JA Company Programme run by the SAME foundation, Genc Basari). GencBizzTech is a distinct program with distinct eligibility (science-high-school-only vs. GencBizz's broader 13-18 lise eligibility) and should NOT be merged with the existing GencBizz record. High relevance for ORYN's core Turkish audience specifically. Recommend a follow-up once the 2027 cycle's official page/calendar goes live, since the calendar graphic could not be read as text this session.
